_: EP 15 — webhooks. The EP 13/14 construction (one continuous vertical strip the camera travels, stations rather than slides, one stroke-icon family, the marquee drag+zoom as the teaching instrument) rebuilt on the DESIGN.md language: gradient-mesh heroes, thin-weight display type with negative tracking, indigo as the only filled CTA colour, tabular figures on every number. The new vocabulary this episode owns is three things: the RIBBON FIELD (the animated 'gg' stripe gradient, full-bleed, behind the title / chapters / end card), the 3D CARD MARQUEE (vertical columns of event cards under a perspective tilt — the firehose you can see), and the HERO CARD (one floating glass panel, one big tabular number, framed the way the reference clip frames it). EVERY NUMBER ON SCREEN IS REAL AND SOURCED: Stripe-Signature is t=<unix>,v1=<hex> HMAC-SHA256 over `${t}.${raw_body}` keyed by whsec_…; the library default tolerance is 5 minutes; Stripe retries with exponential backoff for up to 3 days in live mode; Slack wants 2xx in 3s and retries 3 times; Shopify times out at 5s (1s to connect) and retries 8 times over 4 hours; GitHub wants 2xx in 10s. Ordering is explicitly not guaranteed and delivery is at-least-once — both straight from the docs, both on screen.

_vo: TEACHING FIRST, in the order a working endpoint gets built. Why not polling; the mechanism; the delivery itself; subscribe narrowly; the URL is public; verify the signature; sign the RAW body; check the clock; ack before you work; assume duplicates; assume disorder; assume retries; and finally, keep the sweep. Definition then consequence, one clause per sentence, no hedges. Title and end card carry no line, so the bed lifts.

vo.text:
Watch what polling costs you. You ask every fifteen seconds, all day…
to hear one thing once.

Here is the whole mechanism. The event happens on their side.
They POST it to a URL you gave them.

Read the delivery. It is an ordinary POST.
A signature header, an event id, and the object that changed.

Subscribe to what you handle, and nothing else.
Every extra event type is load you agreed to carry.

Now notice the problem. That URL is public.
Anyone on the internet can POST to it.

So verify the signature. HMAC the timestamp, a dot, and the body…
keyed by your endpoint secret.

Sign the RAW body. Parse the JSON first, re-serialise it, and the bytes change.
Every signature fails.

Check the timestamp too. Five minutes of tolerance is the default.
Older than that, reject the replay.

Return two hundred first. Do the work after.
Slack gives you three seconds. Shopify five. GitHub ten.

Assume you will see an event twice. Delivery is at-least-once.
Record the event id, and skip what you already processed.

Do not trust the order. Events arrive out of sequence.
Reconcile against the object, never against arrival.

A failed delivery comes back. Stripe retries for three days.
Shopify retries eight times in four hours.

So treat webhooks as an optimisation, never as the source of truth.
Keep the sweep. Run it on a schedule.
